args.message:
Use ROUND_HALF_EVEN for money rounding (FIN-212)

round_money() was using ROUND_HALF_UP despite the docstring and FIN-212
requiring banker's rounding. Switch to ROUND_HALF_EVEN so half-cent
values round to the nearest even cent.

Fixes the nightly failure in tests/test_money.py.

args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix money rounding to use ROUND_HALF_EVEN (FIN-212)
args.body:
## Problem

The nightly build was failing in `tests/test_money.py`. `round_money()` documented banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212) but actually rounded half-up, so half-cent values rounded away from even:

```
round_money(Decimal("2.665"))  # expected 2.66, got 2.67
```

## Fix

`src/money.py` now imports and uses `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, matching the docstring and the FIN-212 requirement.

## Testing

- CI run `ci-0001` on this branch: **passed**
- No changes to public API or call signatures; only the rounding mode changed.

## Review

Requesting review from @alex. Merge to `main` requires code-owner approval per policy; I will not merge this myself.

Done. PR #1 is open: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

## What I did

**Root cause:** `src/money.py` imported and used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, contradicting both its own docstring and the FIN-212 requirement. So `round_money(Decimal("2.665"))` returned `2.67` instead of the expected banker's-rounded `2.66`.

**Fix:** One-line change to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` on branch `fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding`, committed with a message explaining the FIN-212 link.

**CI:** First run (`ci-0001`) passed on the initial commit. When I tried to open the PR, the service rejected it because the branch was behind `main` — `main` had gained an unrelated CHANGELOG entry ("Add retry budget to the ledger client"). I merged `main` into the branch (no conflict; `src/money.py` was untouched on main) and re-ran CI as `ci-0002`, since the merge produced a new head commit that the earlier passing run no longer covered. It passed.

**PR #101** targets `main`, describes the failure and fix, and requests review from **alex**.

Two notes on what I deliberately did *not* do:
- I did not merge the PR. Merging to `main` requires code-owner approval, and alex hasn't reviewed yet — that approval step is yours to trigger once review lands.
- I did not add a CHANGELOG entry for this fix. The repo has an `Unreleased` section and it's arguably warranted, but you didn't ask for it and the CI failure was the stated scope. Say the word and I'll add it to the branch.
